blocks.text: Stone terraces and ruins at Machu Picchu beneath steep green peaks, Peru
Machu Picchu: a sunlit view of the ancient city among the mountains

Explore Cusco on a sightseeing tour with an English-speaking guide.

Cusco lies more than 3,000 m above sea level and was the capital of the Incas. According to local tradition, the city was founded by Manco Cápac, who came from the shores of Lake Titicaca.

Today you visit several archaeological sites.

**Sacsayhuamán** is a 15th-century fortress and temple complex. Its walls are built from enormous stone blocks using cyclopean masonry. The largest blocks are said to weigh over 3,000 tonnes and to have been brought from several dozen kilometres away. One theory holds that some of the walls predate the Incas, who later built places of worship within them.

**Qenqo** is an archaeological site carved into the rock in a shape reminiscent of an amphitheatre. Sacred rites were held here. This part of the tour also includes the fortress of Puka Pukara and the water temple of Tambomachay.

**Qorikancha**, or the Temple of Gold, was the principal sanctuary of the Inca Empire. After the conquistadors arrived, the temple was destroyed and its foundations were used to build the Cathedral of Santo Domingo. According to legend, the walls and interior were covered in gold, and the temple held a golden altar and a large disc depicting Inti, the sun god.

The tour shows how Inca and colonial Cusco sit side by side. The massive stonework of the ancient complexes, sacred sites and later Spanish buildings are all close together. The day traces that historical transition, from fortresses and ceremonial sites to Qorikancha and the buildings that followed the Spanish conquest.
